title: MNT Reform 2 · dead 3.3 V rail
description: An open-hardware laptop mainboard (522 parts) that came back from a repair desk: it powers up, but the system never starts. The bench supply is clipped onto the gated input rail. Find out why the 3.3 V rail is missing, fix it, and leave the board clean.
credits: MNT Reform 2 motherboard rev 3.0, designed by MNT Research GmbH. Converted and modified (planted faults) for DEADBOARD.

title: Antmicro baseboard · no 3.3 V, flaky 5 V
description: An open-source carrier board for a compute module (369 parts), fed 12 V at its input. The module will not start: 3.3 V is missing, and the customer says the 5 V rail "sometimes" drops out when the board is handled.
credits: Jetson Nano / Xavier NX baseboard, Copyright (c) 2020-2024 Antmicro, Apache-2.0. Converted and modified (planted faults) for DEADBOARD. Jetson is a trademark of NVIDIA; no endorsement implied.

title: Olimex ESP32-DevKit-LiPo · dead on USB, won't charge
description: A real, sold ESP32 board (50 parts) with a Li-ion charger. The owner says it stopped doing anything on USB after the cable got yanked, and before that the battery "never seemed to charge". No battery is plugged in on your bench.
credits: ESP32-DevKit-LiPo Rev. D, designed by OLIMEX Ltd, hardware Apache-2.0. Converted and modified (planted faults) for DEADBOARD. ESP32 is a trademark of Espressif Systems; no endorsement implied.

title: Olimex ESP32-C3-DevKit-Lipo · hot board, wrong 3.3 V
description: A real, sold ESP32-C3 board (49 parts) back from a small production run: on USB it gets warm and the chip never starts. The assembler says two reels were swapped somewhere on that batch. No battery is plugged in on your bench.
credits: ESP32-C3-DevKit-Lipo Rev. D, designed by OLIMEX Ltd, hardware CERN-OHL-S-2.0. Converted and modified (planted faults) for DEADBOARD. ESP32 is a trademark of Espressif Systems; no endorsement implied.

title: ESP32-C3 Rust board · rails fine, chip asleep
description: A real, sold ESP32-C3 training board (55 parts: sensors, RGB LED, Li-ion charger, USB-C). It came back from a workshop where someone spilled a drink on the bench, and another participant says it "only really worked on the battery" before that. On USB it now stays silent. No battery is plugged in on your bench.
credits: ESP32-C3-DevKit-RUST-1 (Rust ESP Board) rev. 1.2a, Espressif Systems and the esp-rs project, CERN-OHL-P-2.0. Converted and modified (planted faults) for DEADBOARD. ESP32 is a trademark of Espressif Systems; no endorsement implied.

title: Rana Tadpole · dead controller, warm chips, one dead button
description: A real, sold pocket controller for platform fighters (147 parts: RP2040, 20 mouse-switch buttons, USB-C). On USB the computer sees nothing, and the owner says it gets warm in the middle. Is the RP2040 dead? And before it died, one button (SW2) had stopped registering.
credits: Rana Tadpole V2 motherboard, by rana-sylvatica; PCB design by Quark. CERN-OHL-S-2.0. Converted and modified (planted fault) for DEADBOARD; no endorsement implied.

title: Rana Tadpole V1 · dead on USB
description: The first version of a real, sold pocket controller (56 parts: RP2040, 20 mouse-switch buttons). USB comes in from a small breakout board over the flat cable (U2). Plugged in, the computer sees nothing, and nothing gets warm.
credits: Rana Tadpole V1 motherboard, by rana-sylvatica; PCB design by Quark. CERN-OHL-S-2.0. Converted and modified (planted fault) for DEADBOARD; no endorsement implied.
